product_from_film: Voyager presents a prompt-based assistant for creative media work across files and editing tools.
explains_well: A recurring forest project links footage, folders, editing timelines and altered scenery.
unclear: The exact boundary between Voyager, the other displayed tools and generated examples is not clear without narration.
scenario: Organize redwood-forest footage and work on its video and scene variants.
product_clear_basis: A Voyager prompt asks to organize Redwood Forest footage, followed by file windows.

scenes.action: A presenter in a forest gains a large Voyager title. Forest examples carry video, music and games labels; code and a small blue preview follow.
scenes.design: Natural forest imagery, large white title, dark code screen.
scenes.purpose: Introduce broad creative ambition and contrast it with technical work.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–13s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A many-shot gallery gains S-tier Content text. A purple prompt interface replaces it; a request to organize forest footage appears and the send button is isolated.
scenes.design: Dark purple field, white prompt, large translucent cursor.
scenes.purpose: Move from outputs to a specific input task.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 13–25s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Two file windows show forest clips and folders, followed by a scenic editor preview, grey forest model and multitrack video editor. The timeline becomes large before a plus icon.
scenes.design: File thumbnails, many colored timeline strips and grey model geometry.
scenes.purpose: Suggest action across the creative workspace.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 25–38s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Fern and canopy imagery lead to a forest shot with an inline request. Similar tree compositions then gain brighter mist and snow.
scenes.design: Full-frame foliage; small prompt overlay and recognizable trunks.
scenes.purpose: Show variations on the same visual material.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 38–50s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The forest presenter returns; a stack of work windows overlays her, then clears.
scenes.design: Natural green background with dark panels and sketches.
scenes.purpose: Reconnect broad tool coverage to the presenter.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 50–61s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A closer presenter shot gains assistant text and a list of skill paths with small example images. A roda mark and large increasing numerals follow.
scenes.design: Thin serif label, translucent skill rows, large white numbers.
scenes.purpose: Explain reusable skills and add a scale claim; number meaning is unclear from samples.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 61–73s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Forest floor and upward tree views replace the presenter. Voyager title appears over sky, then rests on purple with the website.
scenes.design: Soft sky and dark purple final card.
scenes.purpose: Close with the same forest world and a start link.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 73–84.918s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: The forest links presenter, examples and a practical organize-footage request; later the story broadens to skills.
A presenter appears in a forest; a large Voyager title arrives by 1s. Product function is not yet visible.
Creative media users are implied by video/music/games labels at 5–7s. A concrete assistant task appears at 22s.
The prompt, send button and editor timeline appear at progressively closer scales. Oversized cursor shapes mark actions; exact paths are unresolved.
The gallery becomes a purple workspace near 18s; the scene changes to file windows near 25s. These are sampled state boundaries, not verified cut mechanisms.
Natural greens ground the product in one project; purple glows mark the software layer.
A large readable request anchors meaning, but editor text and skills rows are much denser. The large 100000 figure lacks a visible unit.
The inspected ASR draft provides partial script-role support; recognition limits are recorded in A02. Audible voice characteristics and delivery remain unchecked.
categories.reason: Local draft text was read; no direct listening.

categories.finding: Presenter footage, foliage, rendered-looking forest variants, code, file windows and editing screens are mixed; asset origin is unknown.

categories.finding: Footage organization and forest variation are understandable silently. Claims about harness, integrations and the large number remain uncertain.
Large cursor and isolated send button guide attention. Overlaid windows compete with the presenter in the 54–57s range.
Files, scenic editor, grey 3D scene and video timeline arrive within 13s; the integration story needs labels or a slower example.
categories.experiment: Hold one file-to-timeline result and name what the assistant changed.

categories.finding: The opening promises broad creativity. The prompt and multi-tool examples support that direction, while the final forest returns to the original setting.
The forest and presenter appear intended to make technical creative work feel approachable; no viewer emotion was measured.
Redwood footage and similar forest trees remain traceable across tools. The later robot sketch and brand/number inserts broaden away from that scenario.
A request and subsequent workspace states are shown, but continuous agent execution and genuine integrations are not independently checked.
The real-world forest ties the presenter and product demo together. Purple UI and a large white name alone are less distinctive.
The organize-footage request and folder result are useful. The later number claim needs a label; otherwise it adds little silent meaning.
For Tin, retain one campaign asset across folders, workflow and published preview, with a visible plain-language request.
categories.experiment: Use one campaign’s source files and final preview rather than unrelated output examples.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Carry the same forest project from the real-world setting into the software states.
try: For Tin, open beside a real product, ask for its campaign, then show that same product in the generated asset and workflow output.
Show one source folder and one completed campaign preview with a single large cursor and a label naming the changed state.
lessons.avoid: Showing many creative tools without stating which action the assistant performed.
lessons.open: Narration, audio design, actual integrations, number meaning and exact inter-frame motion remain unverified.

comparison.story: Presenter and media promise → prompt → multi-tool forest work → variants → skills → brand.
comparison.motion: UI scale changes and oversized cursor states; whole film at roughly 1 fps, easing unresolved.
comparison.sound: No validated listening; voice delivery, music, effects and sync unknown.
comparison.texture: Natural forest footage and purple software layer; production and asset sources unknown.
comparison.lesson: Use one visual project as continuity across multiple tools.

sound.detail: The coherent draft introduces Voyager as a creative-work harness, then describes footage review, professional-tool use, generation, iteration, feedback and personalization. Tool/model names have recognition errors; these are spoken claims in a draft, not validated capabilities. No validated listening; delivery, music, effects, mix and synchronization remain unknown.
